'''''Euphorbia dulcis''''', '''sweet spurge''', is a species in the genus ''[[Euphorbia]]'', native to Europe.<ref name="346333-1" >{{cite web |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:346333-1 |title=''Euphorbia dulcis'' L. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=19 September 2020 }}</ref> It is not as acrid as other ''Euphorbia'' species, hence the epithet which means "sweet".<ref>{{Cite book|last=Linnaeus|first=Carl|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/358476#page/469/mode/1up|title=Species Plantarum|publisher=Laurentius Salvius|year=1753|volume=1 |location=Stockholm|pages=457}}</ref> The cultivar 'Chameleon', with purple foliage, is the one most commonly planted in gardens.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Aniśko |first1=Tomasz |date=29 October 2008 |title=When Perennials Bloom: An Almanac for Planning and Planting |publisher=Timber Press |pages=192–193 |isbn=9780881928877 }}</ref>
